title: Microscopy Digital Image Manipulation: The Good, The Bad, and The Unethical
content: Scientific digital imaging is a small subset of digital imaging. This is an important distinction, because digital imaging has a lot of capabilities for making astonishing images. However, in scientific imaging, most of these capabilities should be avoided. For a microscopist, the image is the primary data. Thus, any alteration you make in your image in some way alters your data. Image alterations are not all bad. Specific alterations can help you visualize components of the image that were not readily apparent, can help highlight key points in the image, can resolve structures not visible without manipulation. On the other hand, some manipulations can obscure key information, distort relationships, and create structures that did not exist in the original object. It is thus imperative that the microscopist understands as thoroughly as possible what any manipulation algorithm will do to their image data. Moreover, during analysis they need to take into consideration how their image might have been altered during data acquisition or processing. Finally, they should avoid any manipulation whose results cannot be adequately accounted for during analysis.
